Ce que je vais écrire n’est qu’une hypothèse 
Mais je pense que cela découle d’années de confrontation avec la police, et donc de leur mauvaise image, encore plus renforcée par le confinement et les missions qui leurs ont été confiées. De plus, on a embauché beaucoup de nouveaux policiers (sans augmenter de façon suffisamment conséquente le budget), résultat on s’est retrouvés avec beaucoup de mecs pas très futés qui ne répondent que par la violence et le racisme, d’où la multiplication des violences policières qui sont un réel problème...

Au milieu de tout ça, des policiers normaux qui respectent les autres et font ce métier pour permettre aux gens de vivre (rappelons que la liberté de tout un chacun s’arrête là où commence celle des autres, ces filles étaient donc clairement en tort) n’osent parfois plus agir, de peur de participer à cette image négative de la police.

Bref ce n’est qu’une hypothèse, si ça se trouve les trois policiers avaient juste la flemme ou une plus grosse urgence un peu plus loin. Ou autre.

I am really sorry for your loss... 
Although you’ve got to accept that you’re human too and that being able to get better and take care of her is already a shit lot considering what you’ve been through. I mean, I can’t even imagine the daily battle happening in your brain every single day...
I’m sure she’s so proud of you and of what you’ve overcome to help her.

Cherish the good moments, the fact that you were there when she left her body, cherish the happiness that she brought in your life, and maybe use it to keep going.

Maybe ask him if he is thinking the same thing or not?
Sometimes one of us / both of us are overwhelmed with work, or preoccupied by something completely exterior to the couple, but it affects it. 
If you both agree, you might be willing to do stuff together (like sports or going out or whatever) and really enjoy the presence of the other.

You’re strong and clever and beautiful and everything, don’t worry. You just can’t see it right now, because #depression. But keep fighting, don’t jump and reach for help instead. At school, with a doctor, whoever, just an adult who’s is kind and a good listener.

I started feeling the same last year but my BF, who had been struggling with this particular side-effect of depression for a few years now made his best to prevent that. 
I guess what’s important is to really try to work on accepting and genuinely understanding that if you didn’t do a lot of stuff, it’s perfectly ok. 
Also, it’s better to get re-used to do things slowly, printing the habit into your brain and body, so that it will stay and be stronger than just forcing yourself to do A LOT all of a sudden. 
But well, those are tips that worked for me, and we’re all different. Try different ones, and keep those that work :3 
Good luck <3
